official.deadline_central_display: 1 April 2027 (first application cycle closes; it opens 1 January 2027)
official.deadline_note: A*STAR publishes two fixed cycles a year - first cycle opens 1 January and closes 1 April, second cycle opens 14 July and closes 1 October - giving day and month but no year; with the second 2026 cycle having closed on 1 October 2026, the next closing date is 1 April 2027. A*GA may consider off-cycle applications on a case-by-case basis.
official.application_cycle: Two application cycles per year (1 January - 1 April; 14 July - 1 October); interviews mid-April to May or mid-October to mid-November, outcomes from mid-June or from December
official.status_note: The second 2026 cycle closed on 1 October 2026 and the A*STAR careers postings for both tracks currently show as unavailable between cycles; the next cycle opens 1 January 2027 with interviews mid-April to May 2027 and outcomes from mid-June 2027.
benefits: Monthly sustenance allowance, inclusive of CPF contribution
Other allowances including settling-in allowance, computer allowance and conference allowance
Participation in Vista, A*STAR Graduate Academy's developmental programme series for scholars
eligibility: Be Singaporean or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR); foreigners who are non-SPRs and with outstanding track records may be considered on an exceptional basis, and non-Singaporeans are required to have obtained Singapore citizenship prior to the commencement of the fellowship
Have completed a PhD within the last 4 years (applicants in the final stages of their PhD may apply, but their AIF award is confirmed only upon conferment of the PhD degree)
Not have existing bonds to any institution
AIF (Research): possess excellent publication records and have applied or be applying for a relevant postdoctoral position at a top overseas university/laboratory
AIF (Innovation): demonstrate strong aptitude and aspiration to pursue roles in innovation and entrepreneurship (I&E), preferably with good publication records

Mid-Term AIF (Research) only: be Singaporean, be enrolled at a top overseas university/lab at the point of scholarship application, and have the current postdoctoral supervisor as at least 1 of the 2 academic referees
requirements: Propose a research topic aligned to A*STAR's research direction and of relevance and value to the A*STAR Research Institutes

Contact an overseas university/institution supervisor to establish a project proposal before applying, as the AIF award is conditional upon having a confirmed place at the approved overseas university or institution
Seek endorsement from the proposed A*STAR Research Institute supervisor and the Executive Director for the 3-year service commitment before the first round of interview
Seek A*STAR's written permission before changing the research project or before extending the postdoctoral training
Upon completion of the postdoctoral research training, contribute to A*STAR's research institutes and/or relevant organisations for 3 years
documents: CV, which the official page says to have ready before creating an account to apply for the fellowship
All required application documents submitted through the A*STAR careers application for the chosen track, as the application is reviewed upon submission of the complete set
Two academic referees, with Mid-Term AIF (Research) applicants required to name their current postdoctoral supervisor as at least 1 of the 2
selection_criteria: Applications are reviewed upon submission of all required documents, and shortlisted applicants attend at least 2 rounds of interviews, plus other tests where applicable
First interview round: 15 minutes to present the proposed research project followed by 15 minutes of Q&A
The proposed overseas university/institution should be a leading institution in the proposed research area
Processing takes up to 5 months from submission of the complete application to notification of the outcome
coverage: Monthly sustenance allowance, inclusive of CPF contribution
Settling-in allowance, computer allowance and conference allowance
application_method: Apply online through the A*STAR careers posting 'Scholar, A*STAR International Fellowship (Research)' or 'Scholar, A*STAR International Fellowship (Innovation)' on careers.a-star.edu.sg, one posting per track

Attend at least 2 rounds of interviews and any other tests where applicable; candidates overseas or otherwise unable to attend in person for valid reasons may submit a written request to attend virtually
Successful candidates are notified by email, with outcomes from mid-June for the first cycle and from December for the second cycle
official.application_route: Apply online via the A*STAR careers posting for your chosen track, after securing a proposed overseas project and host and before the cycle closes.
official.citizenship_residency: Be Singaporean or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR); non-SPR foreigners with outstanding track records may be considered exceptionally, and non-Singaporeans must obtain Singapore citizenship before the fellowship commences
official.international_eligibility: Only on an exceptional basis - non-Singaporeans must take up Singapore citizenship before the post-doctoral training commences
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The research topic must be aligned to A*STAR's research direction and of relevance and value to the A*STAR Research Institutes, within A*STAR's Biomedical or Science & Engineering research areas (the published area list is not exhaustive)
official.research_requirement: Yes - a project proposal established with an overseas university/institution supervisor is required before applying, and AIF (Research) additionally requires excellent publication records plus a postdoctoral position at, or application to, a top overseas university/laboratory
official.duration: Up to 2 years of overseas postdoctoral research training, followed by a 3-year service commitment in Singapore
official.description: The A*STAR International Fellowship is a prestigious scholarship designed to support early-career researchers, giving successful applicants up to 2 years of overseas postdoctoral training in leading overseas universities, research institutions or overseas deep-tech startups which are portfolio companies of top-tier venture capital/builder firms, in either a Research or an Innovation track, before they return to contribute to A*STAR's mission and Singapore's R&D ecosystem.

monthly allowance rates for Singapore Permanent Residents (only the Singapore Citizen rate of S$5,000 is published)
verification.notes: Monthly allowance, coverage items, eligibility, cycle dates, service commitment and interview process were read from A*STAR's own AIF page and its on-page FAQ on 10 October 2026; the careers postings for both tracks were unavailable between cycles at that time.

applicant_utility.summary: The AIF pays a flat S$5,000 a month plus a separate sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF, an annual return airfare, settling-in, computer and conference allowances, and annual personal insurance, but it does not fund your overseas university's research costs or any support for spouse or family. The application hinges on a concrete overseas host: you need a leading-institution supervisor, a project that maps onto A*STAR's biomedical or science-and-engineering priorities, and endorsement from your future A*STAR Research Institute supervisor and its Executive Director before interview round one. File inside the 1 January - 1 April window (or 14 July - 1 October), expect at least two interview rounds including a 15-minute project pitch, and allow up to five months to a decision.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singaporean or Singapore PR researchers within four years of their PhD who already have, or can quickly secure, a postdoc place at a leading overseas lab and are willing to bond three years to A*STAR afterwards.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the overseas host first - the award is conditional on a confirmed place at an approved overseas institution, so lock in a supervisor and project before the cycle opens
Have your CV ready before creating the A*STAR careers account, and submit every required document at once because review only starts on a complete submission
Get the A*STAR Research Institute supervisor and the Executive Director to endorse the 3-year service commitment before the first interview round
Rehearse a tight 15-minute project presentation with Q&A, and prepare for a second interview round and any additional tests
Confirm with A*GA who funds research consumables and fees at the host, since A*STAR explicitly leaves those to the overseas university
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a confirmed place at an approved overseas institution or without a topic tied to A*STAR's research areas
Missing the A*STAR Research Institute and Executive Director endorsement before interview round one
Non-SPR applicants who cannot complete Singapore citizenship conversion before the training commences
Existing bonds to another institution, which are disqualifying outright
Applying late in the window and then waiting out the up-to-5-month processing period
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Overseas research consumables and research-related fees, which must be supported by the overseas university, plus all spouse and family costs; the monthly allowance is flat and does not scale with the host country's cost of living.
document_audit: The full document list lives inside the A*STAR careers application portal rather than on the public programme page, so check it as soon as the cycle opens
Only the Singapore Citizen monthly rate of S$5,000 is published - Singapore PRs should confirm their own rate with A*STAR Graduate Academy
The careers postings are open only during the application windows, so prepare the CV and host details in advance of 1 January

Innovation-track applicants must point to a placement at a portfolio company of a top-tier VC/builder firm, or a VC/VB firm with an entrepreneur-in-residence programme - A*STAR publishes a partner list to check against
alerts: Two hard windows a year: 1 January - 1 April and 14 July - 1 October; off-cycle applications are only considered case by case
Non-citizens must obtain Singapore citizenship before the postdoctoral training begins, which adds months to the timeline
A 3-year service commitment at A*STAR's research institutes and/or relevant organisations follows the training
Changing the research project or extending the training both require A*STAR's written permission in advance
Mid-term applicants (Research track only) must already be enrolled overseas and must use their current postdoc supervisor as one of the two referees
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through the A*STAR careers posting for your track, wait for the document review, then clear at least two interview rounds before an outcome up to five months later.

official.deadline_central_display: 19 March 2027 (AY2027 admission; Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level and IB Diploma routes)
official.deadline_note: There is no single deadline: the scholarship application period equals the admission application period for each qualification route. For AY2027, NUS High School Diploma applicants close on 20 January 2027 (photo and appraisal by 27 January), Singapore polytechnic diploma applicants on 21 February 2027 (photo and appraisal by 28 February), and Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level and IB Diploma applicants on 19 March 2027 (photo and appraisal by 26 March). Year 12 equivalent / international qualification applicants apply within their own admission window, which runs from 15 October 2026 to 20 January 2027 or 19 March 2027 depending on the qualification. Applications submitted after the closing date are not considered.
official.application_cycle: AY2027 undergraduate admission intake; international-qualification applications open 15 October 2026, with scholarship interviews between March and May 2027
official.status_note: NTU's Important dates page publishes the AY2027 cycle: the international-qualifications window opens 15 October 2026 and NUS High School opens 1 December 2026, while A-Level applicants apply from results release day to 19 March 2027 and polytechnic diploma applicants from 1 February 2027; scholarship selection interviews run between March and May 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full coverage of subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant).
benefits: Full coverage of subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant)
Living allowance of S$5,000 per academic year
No bond is attached to the Nanyang Merit Scholarship apart from the three-year bond applicable to all Singapore PRs and international students under the MOE Tuition Grant Scheme
eligibility: Successful awardees should read a full-time undergraduate degree programme; the scholarship will cover the years of study at NTU

Possess outstanding academic achievements in the Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' level, Diploma awarded by a polytechnic in Singapore, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent qualifications
requirements: Maintain a minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 3.5 over 5.0, with academic performance reviewed every semester
Not hold concurrently any other scholarships, bursaries, university loans or awards without the approval of the University
Take on the role of student ambassador, or any other similar representative role representing the university in publicity talks and receiving guests, as and when called upon

Maintain satisfactory progress and conduct, as the scholarship may be withdrawn at any time if the University deems these unsatisfactory, with repayment imposed if the scholarship is terminated prematurely
documents: Online scholarship application form, logged in with the application number assigned by the NTU admission application
Personal Essay of not more than 250 words on the compulsory topic included in the scholarship application form
Recent passport-size digital photograph uploaded after the application form is submitted
Online referee's appraisal completed by a school teacher who is not a family member or relative, submitted within 7 days of the scholarship application (only one appraisal may support an application)
selection_criteria: Outstanding academic achievements in the qualifying school qualifications, good co-curricular records, and good leadership qualities and potential
Only shortlisted applicants are informed by email and invited to a scholarship selection interview, held between March and May
Outcomes are usually communicated within 2 to 3 weeks after the interview, and the scholarship offer must be accepted by the stipulated deadline
coverage: Full coverage of subsidised tuition fees (after Tuition Grant)
Living allowance of S$5,000 per academic year
$4000 Travel Grant, one-off, for overseas exposure
application_method: Submit the online NTU admission application first, then open the scholarship form via the 'Apply for Scholarship' link at the end of the admission application, logging in with the assigned application number

Complete the form including the compulsory 250-word Personal Essay, then upload the passport-size photo and forward the generated referee URL to a school teacher together with the NTU application number and date of birth
Applicants with Year 12 equivalent results apply through the separate international-qualification portal with their assigned application number before that qualification's application closing date
official.application_route: Apply for NTU admission first, then file the online Nanyang Merit Scholarship form with your application number, essay, passport photo and teacher appraisal.
official.study_mode: Full-time undergraduate degree programme at NTU
official.citizenship_residency: Open to all nationalities; Singapore Permanent Residents and international students remain subject to the three-year MOE Tuition Grant Scheme bond
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is open to all nationalities
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction is published; the award is open to outstanding freshmen entering NTU's full-time undergraduate programmes, with Medicine and Renaissance Engineering Programme applicants informed of their scholarship outcome by the school instead
official.duration: Up to the normal programme duration at NTU, conditional on good academic performance and exemplary conduct, with CGPA reviewed every semester
official.description: The Nanyang Merit Scholarship is awarded to outstanding freshmen pursuing full-time undergraduate programmes in NTU, covering subsidised tuition fees after the Tuition Grant and adding a S$5,000 annual living allowance and a one-off S$4,000 travel grant for overseas exposure.

not_confirmed: english_requirement - the scholarship page publishes no English test requirement; English requirements for entry are set separately by NTU admissions
a single deadline date, since the scholarship deadline tracks the admission deadline for each qualification route

full funding status, since hostel accommodation, miscellaneous fees and living costs beyond the S$5,000 annual allowance are not covered and tuition coverage applies to the subsidised fee after the MOE Tuition Grant
verification.notes: Benefits, eligibility, terms, documents and interview timing were read from NTU's Nanyang Merit Scholarship page; the AY2027 cycle dates were taken from NTU's Important dates page and the process steps from NTU's Scholarship Application Process page, all on 10 October 2026.

applicant_utility.summary: The award waives your subsidised tuition, that is the balance after the MOE Tuition Grant, and adds S$5,000 a year of living allowance plus a one-off S$4,000 travel grant, with no NTU bond of its own - but Singapore PRs and international students still take on the three-year MOE Tuition Grant bond. You must apply for NTU admission first, because the scholarship form only opens behind the application number that admission gives you, and your school teacher has to file the online appraisal within 7 days of your submission. Keeping the award depends on a CGPA of 3.5 out of 5.0 reviewed every semester, on not holding another award without permission, and on doing ambassador duties when asked.
applicant_utility.best_fit: School leavers of any nationality with top A-Level, Singapore polytechnic diploma, NUS High School, IB or Year 12 equivalent results plus a solid co-curricular and leadership record who want tuition covered at NTU without an NTU-specific bond.
application_readiness_checklist: File the NTU admission application first and keep the application number to hand, since the scholarship form is only reachable through it
Draft the compulsory 250-word Personal Essay ahead of time, because the form fixes the topic
Brief your school teacher early and send the referee URL together with your NTU application number and date of birth - they have 7 days and only one appraisal counts
Have a recent passport-size digital photograph ready to upload immediately after submitting the form
Decide on the MOE Tuition Grant before accepting an offer, since PRs and international students who decline it are charged the full non-subsidised fee the scholarship does not cover
common_rejection_risks: Waiting for the admission offer before opening the scholarship form, when the scholarship deadline is the admission deadline and both must be filed in the same window
A teacher appraisal that is never submitted or lands late - the 7-day window is strict and only one appraisal supports the file
Holding another scholarship, bursary, university loan or award without the University's approval
Dropping below a CGPA of 3.5, which is reviewed every semester and can end the award
Missing the March-May interview because shortlist notification is by email and only shortlisted applicants are told
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Miscellaneous fees, hostel or accommodation, meals and personal spending beyond the S$5,000 annual living allowance; the S$4,000 travel grant is a one-off sum rather than a per-trip budget.
document_audit: Submitting the form is not a complete application - the passport photo and the teacher appraisal are separate follow-up steps
Year 12 equivalent and international-qualification applicants use a different portal and a different closing date from A-Level, polytechnic, NUS High School and IB applicants
Medicine and Renaissance Engineering Programme applicants receive their scholarship outcome from the school rather than through the general email
The referee must not be a family member or relative, and only one online appraisal may be submitted per application
alerts: AY2027 deadlines differ by qualification: 20 January 2027 for NUS High School Diploma, 21 February 2027 for a Singapore polytechnic diploma, and 19 March 2027 for A-Level and IB, with photo and appraisal due about a week later
Shortlisted applicants are emailed by mid-May, so be ready to attend an interview at short notice - and one interview may cover several scholarships
Accepting the MOE Tuition Grant obliges Singapore PRs and international students to work for a Singapore entity for three years after graduation
Terminating the scholarship early triggers repayment, and the University can withdraw it for unsatisfactory progress or behaviour
If unsuccessful, short-term scholarships and financial aid schemes remain open to current students
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: File the admission application, open the scholarship form with your application number, submit the essay and form, upload the photo, get the teacher appraisal filed within 7 days, then attend an interview if shortlisted.
